  - New H3 added: `### LEADING CANONICAL — Postgres EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ts) → Trino to_unixtime(ts) (Trino's EXTRACT has NO EPOCH field)` at r23. Content:
    * Keyword anchors blockquote: EXTRACT EPOCH Trino, timestamp to epoch seconds Trino, to_unixtime, Postgres EXTRACT EPOCH equivalent, convert timestamp to unix seconds, epoch from timestamp Trino, seconds since epoch Trino, porting Postgres EXTRACT(EPOCH) to Trino. Verified date 2026-06-07.
    * One-fact summary: Postgres EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ts) returns DOUBLE seconds (incl. fractional); Trino's EXTRACT does NOT support EPOCH; only YEAR/QUARTER/MONTH/WEEK/DAY/DOW/DOY/HOUR/MINUTE/SECOND/TIMEZONE_* are supported (verbatim list). Trino-correct: to_unixtime(timestamp) → double (verbatim signature) returns epoch SECONDS as DOUBLE; inverse from_unixtime(seconds) returns timestamp(3) with time zone.
    * Worked example: Postgres EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM occurred_at) (fails in Trino) → Trino to_unixtime(occurred_at) — DOUBLE seconds; CAST(to_unixtime AS BIGINT) — whole seconds; CAST(to_unixtime * 1000 AS BIGINT) — epoch MILLISECONDS (cross-ref r13).
    * Prefer date_diff(unit, a, b) over subtracting to_unixtime for elapsed-time (BIGINT integer + named unit + cleaner).
    * 4-row DO-NOT-WRITE: (1) 'Trino supports EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ts)' FALSE — no EPOCH field; (2) 'to_unixtime returns milliseconds' FALSE — returns SECONDS as DOUBLE; for ms multiply by 1000; (3) 'EXTRACT works the same on Trino and Postgres' FALSE — EPOCH is Postgres-specific; (4) 'unix_timestamp(ts) is the Trino function' FALSE — that's Spark/Hive; Trino is to_unixtime.
    * Cross-refs: r13 from_unixtime SECONDS-vs-MS year-52000 pitfall + r07 now() canonical + r27 §4.2-NOW + r13 Postgres date-function porting table.
